classes.name: Sewing 101 - Practical Sewing Fundamentals - 2 Days -$145
classes.description:
Sewing 101 - Practical Sewing Fundamentals - $145
2 Days - 3 Hours each day
 
The broad goal of this course is to help students cultivate the skills, knowledge, and attitudes necessary to start and troubleshoot basic sewing projects. Students are not expected to have any prior textile experience and the information should be a helpful refresher for anyone looking to get back into the textile shop.

This course is designed to give students hands-on experience with the home sewing machine and work on a project.
 
At the end of the course, students will be able to:

-Learn, have fun, and be inspired in the textile shop while also managing expectations on new projects
-Be a steward of the textile shop
-Identify different types of fabrics and their appropriateness for different projects
-Perform basic hand sewing techniques / repairs including measuring, cutting, pinning, and stitching fabric
-Set up and operate a home sewing machine
-Plan and carry out a sewing project

This class counts as a safety checkout for members to use the Roundhouse Heavy Duty Singer machines.

Max 4 students

classes.name: Woodworking Through ASL: Butcher Board Workshop for the Deaf and Hard of Hearing - 2 Days - $115 - all materials included
classes.description:
Woodworking Through ASL: Butcher Board Workshop for the Deaf and Hard of Hearing - $115 all materials included

2 sessions, 3 hours each day

This two-day class will walk you through all the steps in making a beautiful butcher block cutting board, taught through American Sign Language (ASL). This class will provide an introduction to the Wood Shop using the Butcher Block cutting board as a project.

The course will cover the different types of wood you can use and address the difference between domestic and exotic, light and dark wood species. You will be instructed on how to prepare your wood, including the cutting, milling, and attachment.

The 2nd class will be focused on finishing: planner action, orbit sander, mineral oil, cleaning, how to attach handles, maintenance, and a short quiz about wood species.

The material used for the class: dark walnut, redwood, poplar, maple, mahogany, white oak, and possibly cedar and hickory.

Specs for butcher block: roughly 12" by 22 “and roughly 1 1/4 thickness.

Those new to woodworking or looking for a refresher are welcome. This is a project-based class and does not qualify as a wood shop safety checkout for members. Those wishing to use the wood shop independently without prior skills will need to sign up for a Wood Shop 101 before becoming a member.

Maximum 5 Students.
